subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a core global `openclaw agent --dry-run` tool-execution mode, and if so what exact CLI/Gateway scope, hook ordering, redaction, read/write policy, and client-tool behavior should it guarantee?
rationale: This changes a security-facing execution boundary and adds a new CLI flag; automation can prove the gap exists but cannot choose the product and security semantics safely.

options.title: Specify core dry-run contract
options.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-owned design that defines the agent-wide dry-run contract before a PR implements it.

options.title: Keep dry-run scoped
options.body: Decide that previews should remain command-specific for now, such as cron, doctor, config, and update, and do not add a global agent mode.

options.title: Prototype through hooks first
options.body: Use before-tool-call hooks or a plugin experiment to gather behavior evidence before promoting a stable core CLI flag.

recommendation.title: Specify core dry-run contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a maintainer-owned design that defines the agent-wide dry-run contract before a PR implements it.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central agent/tool files route through recent `jalehman` agents/session work, making this the best available code-history owner for the decision packet.
